# Ingest worker recovery

The worker stopped writing checkpoints after the deploy.

## 1. Inspect the running process

$ systemctl status ingest-worker --no-pager
$ ps -o pid,user,args -C ingest-worker

The unit runs as ingest. Any permission fix must work for that user, not for your shell.

## 2. Read the unit and the recent log

$ systemctl cat ingest-worker
$ journalctl -u ingest-worker -n 50 --no-pager

Look for the failing path and the first error, not the last line of the trace.

## 3. Check the data directory

$ stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' /var/lib/ingest

The directory is owned by root with mode 755, so the ingest user cannot create a checkpoint file.

## 4. Grant the smallest access that works

$ chown -R ingest:ingest /var/lib/ingest
$ chmod 2770 /var/lib/ingest

The group needs write access, and new files should stay in the ingest group. No other user needs access.

## 5. Restart and verify

$ systemctl restart ingest-worker
$ systemctl is-active ingest-worker
$ journalctl -u ingest-worker --since '2 minutes ago' --no-pager

A returned restart is not proof of health. The unit must be active and the log must show a new checkpoint.
